Continue to identify the tiles as shown above. On the grid below, write the letters A, B, C, or D to make a symmetrical pattern where PQ and RS would be lines of symmetry. Arrange the tiles to make a pattern.

item.figure_description:
At the top, four square tiles labeled A, B, C, and D are shown in a row. Each tile is divided conceptually into four smaller quadrants:
- Tile A: A shaded black triangle in the upper-left corner (formed by the diagonal connecting the midpoint of the top edge and the midpoint of the left edge) and a solid black square in the lower-right quadrant.
- Tile B: A shaded black triangle in the upper-right corner and a solid black square in the lower-left quadrant.
- Tile C: A solid black square in the upper-left quadrant and a shaded black triangle in the lower-right corner.
- Tile D: A solid black square in the upper-right quadrant and a shaded black triangle in the lower-left corner.

Below is a 4-by-4 square grid of 16 unit squares, divided into four 2-by-2 quadrants by a vertical line PQ and a horizontal line RS. P is at the top of the vertical line, Q is at the bottom; R is at the left of the horizontal line, S is at the right. Four squares are already labeled:
- Row 1 (top), column 1 (left): 'D'
- Row 2, column 4 (right): 'C'
- Row 3, column 2: 'B'
- Row 4 (bottom), column 3: 'A'
The remaining 12 squares are blank.

reference_items.stem: Which picture shows that 2/5 is equivalent to 4/10 ?

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: 2-by-5 grid with 5 squares shaded in a checkerboard pattern]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Rectangle with 2 solid circles and 3 open circles]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four labeled options (A, B, C, D):
- Option A shows a rectangle divided into a 2-by-5 grid of 10 equal squares. The two squares in the first column and the two squares in the fifth column are completely shaded black (4 of 10 squares shaded).
- Option B shows a rectangle divided into a 2-by-5 grid of 10 equal squares. The top-left square (row 1, column 1) and bottom-right square (row 2, column 5) are shaded black (2 of 10 squares shaded).
- Option C shows a rectangle divided into a 2-by-5 grid of 10 equal squares. In the top row, the 1st, 3rd, and 5th squares are shaded black; in the bottom row, the 2nd and 4th squares are shaded black (5 of 10 squares shaded in a checkerboard pattern).
- Option D shows a rectangular box containing five small circles scattered inside: two circles are solid black and three circles are open white circles with a black outline.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

step1.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's step 1 parameter d1? In the GPCM, b - d1 is the ability at which earning the first point becomes more likely than earning no point, so a higher d1 means that this point is earned at a lower ability; the steps sum to 0. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
